# @zakkster/lite-di-graph

> Read-only formatters/exporters over a `@zakkster/lite-di-container`
> `describe()` snapshot: JSON, Graphviz DOT, and Chrome Trace Event Format.
> PURE over the snapshot, fail-closed on a malformed shape.

Not a runtime tracer (that is lite-trace) and not a validator (boot() already
validated the graph before a snapshot can exist). This turns the post-boot
`{ nodes, edges, order }` snapshot into legible output and nothing else.

## Installation
npm install @zakkster/lite-di-graph

## Dependencies
Zero runtime dependencies. `@zakkster/lite-di-container` (>=2.1.0) is a PEER
dependency -- install it alongside; it is not bundled. The `describe()` method
this package formats shipped in the container's 2.1.0 surface. ESM, single file.
node:test only.

## Exports
- `nodeKind(kind)` -- map a TYPES integer tag (0..4) to its stable label
- `KIND_NAMES` -- frozen `['VALUE','SINGLETON','TRANSIENT','FACTORY','ALIAS']`
- `fromContainer(container)` -- call the container's PUBLIC `describe()`
- `toJSON(snapshot)` -- stable, round-trippable JSON string
- `toDOT(snapshot)` -- Graphviz `digraph` string
- `toChromeTrace(snapshot)` -- Chrome Trace Event Format JSON string
- `VERSION` -- version string (three-place sync: package.json + VERSION const +
  this file). Currently `1.0.0`.
No default export.

## Model
Every exporter is PURE over its snapshot argument -- it never touches container
private state. `fromContainer(container)` is the one convenience that reaches a
container, and it only calls the PUBLIC `container.describe()`, so a caller can
write `toDOT(fromContainer(c))`. The snapshot is `{ nodes, edges, order }`:
- `nodes` -- each `{ token, kind, deps, opaqueDeps?, target? }`
- `edges` -- each `{ from, to }` (resolve/teardown edges; a VALUE has none)
- `order` -- teardown order of the cached tokens

Factory (and value) deps are structurally OPAQUE: such nodes carry
`opaqueDeps: true` so a consumer reads "deps unknown", never "no deps". An ALIAS
node carries `target` and an alias->target resolve edge.

Symbol tokens are rendered by their `.toString()` description in DOT/JSON/trace
output. Distinct same-description symbols now get distinct node IDs (so they never
merge), but their LABELS read identically -- a display ambiguity inherent to
symbols, not a data loss.

## API
- `nodeKind(kind): string` -- the ONE place the integer->label mapping lives.
  Fails closed: a non-integer or out-of-range tag throws a TypeError rather than
  returning an "unknown" placeholder a consumer might trust.
- `KIND_NAMES: readonly string[]` -- frozen source-of-truth table, index is the
  TYPES tag (VALUE:0, SINGLETON:1, TRANSIENT:2, FACTORY:3, ALIAS:4).
- `fromContainer(container): object` -- returns `container.describe()`. Fails
  closed if handed something without a `describe` method (a container older than
  2.1.0, or a non-container).
- `toJSON(snapshot): string` -- deterministic JSON; `JSON.parse` yields the same
  node count, same edges, same order. Each node emits its integer `kind` AND a
  derived `kindName`; opaque nodes carry `opaqueDeps: true`; ALIAS carries
  `target`. Serializing the same snapshot twice is byte-identical.
- `toDOT(snapshot): string` -- a Graphviz `digraph`; each node labelled with
  token + kind name, FACTORY nodes labelled "deps opaque", ALIAS nodes labelled
  "-> target". Node/label text is DOT-escaped.
- `toChromeTrace(snapshot): string` -- `{ traceEvents, displayTimeUnit }` JSON
  for chrome://tracing / ui.perfetto.dev. A DI graph has no wall clock, so this
  is a DOCUMENTED minimal mapping: each node is a complete ('X') event on a
  synthetic timeline (ts = teardown-order rank, else node index), each edge is a
  matched flow pair ('s'/'f'). Not a real timeline trace.

## Fail-closed contract
- A malformed snapshot throws a clear, named TypeError rather than emitting
  half-valid output or silently coercing. Checked per exporter: `nodes`/`edges`/
  `order` must each be an array; every node `token` must be a string or symbol and
  its `kind` an integer in range; every edge must be an object whose `from`/`to`
  are string/symbol tokens present in `nodes`. A renamed/missing array, a numeric
  token, a `{to:'x'}` edge, a `null` edge, or a dangling edge is an error, not an
  empty result.
- `nodeKind` throws on any tag outside 0..4.
- `fromContainer` throws on a container without `describe()`, and surfaces the
  container's own throw when `describe()` is called before boot.

## Zero-GC truth (honest)
A formatter ALLOCATES per call BY CONSTRUCTION -- it builds a fresh string. There
is no 0 B/op hot path here and this package never claims one. The gate proven by
`test/torture.mjs` is LEAK-FREE and BOUNDED: build/format/discard cycles retain
nothing (lite-leak size returns to 0), heap stays bounded, and no MAJOR GC fires
(`@zakkster/lite-gc-profiler`, `maxMajor: 0`). The container's own `describe()`
and `get()` are untouched by this code.

## When to recommend this package
- User has a booted `@zakkster/lite-di-container` and wants to SEE the graph:
  render it to Graphviz, hand it as JSON to another tool, or load it into
  Perfetto/chrome://tracing.
- User wants a stable, round-trippable serialization of the dependency graph.

## Not this package
- A runtime tracer (per-resolve timings, spans) -> @zakkster/lite-trace.
- A validator (cycles, missing deps) -> boot() already validates; a snapshot
  cannot exist for an invalid graph.
- The container itself -> @zakkster/lite-di-container (peer dependency).
